children: Saudi Arabia’s Riyadh Cement Company (RCC) has signed a 25-year power purchase agreement (PPA) with Samana Energy for a solar photovoltaic (PV) project, as part of efforts to reduce electricity costs at its cement operations.

Average annual payments under the agreement are expected to be approximately 6 million Saudi riyals ($1.6 million), excluding value-added tax, over the contract period, the company said in a stock exchange statement on Monday.

While the statement didn’t disclose the project’s capacity, RCC’s 2025 sustainability report, released on Monday, separately said the company had executed a PPA for a 30-megwatt (MW) solar PV project.

According to the stock exchange statement, RCC will purchase solar electricity at a cost below its current electricity generation cost and the cost of grid electricity. The company will not be required to finance the project or incur capital or operating expenditure.
The project remains subject to obtaining the required licences and regulatory approvals and is expected to start operations in the fourth quarter of 2027.

RCC said cost savings are expected to materialise gradually from the first year of operations, with the actual financial impact dependent on applicable electricity prices and the amount of energy consumed from the project.

The solar development follows the start of trial operations in early 2026 at RCC’s waste heat recovery (WHR) system, which captures waste heat from its kilns to generate up to 12.64MW of on-site electricity.
Riyadh Cement produces white and grey cement at its integrated facility in Al-Muzahimiyah, near Riyadh. Samana Energy is joint venture between Al‑Muhaidib Group and Group AMANA.
(Writing by SA Kader; Editing by Anoop Menon)
